checks: Start with any r+1 affinely independent members of A. Every later insertion is a distinct point, and the current hull remains full dimensional throughout.

For an exterior insertion, parameterize each ray from the new apex through the old polytope. The largest entry parameter among the initially violated facet inequalities is attained by one of those finitely many inequalities. The first entry therefore belongs to a strictly visible facet, even if it also lies on a facet coplanar with the apex. The cones over the inherited boundary triangulations cover the added region and are full dimensional. Their common rays have a unique first-entry point, so their intersections are the cones over common base faces or the common apex alone. Their intersection with the old hull is their base.

For an insertion into the old hull, the minimal face F has m≥1. In each incident full simplex, its m+1 facets missing F each omit a vertex of F. The new apex has positive barycentric coefficient at that vertex, so each cone is full dimensional. Restrictions agree on common faces containing F and preserve faces missing F. Purity gives at least one incident full simplex even on the boundary, and m≥1 preserves every old vertex and strictly increases the full-simplex count. This includes the interval case r=1.

The affine basis consumes r+1 points and contributes one simplex. Each of the |A|−(r+1) remaining points adds at least one full simplex, giving |A|−r. The absolute determinant of lattice coordinates of the r edge differences is a positive integer; the linear lattice chart multiplies volume by v and the standard simplex has volume 1/r!.

readability: The exterior-ray argument and the subdivision at the relative interior of a boundary face are compressed. Reading them in the simplicial complex, every boundary face is incident to a full simplex and the cones agree on shared faces. No added assumption is needed.
